Synergistic

/sin-er-JIS-tik/ · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Synergistic means producing a combined effect greater than the sum of the parts' separate effects — the pieces accomplish more together than their individual results could ever add up to alone

Synergistic means producing a combined effect greater than the sum of each part's separate effects. The farmer's synergistic rotation of corn and beans left the soil richer than either crop could have managed alone, and both harvests grew larger every year.

Worked Example

When the middle school scheduled its robotics club right after the new coding elective, the pairing proved synergistic: students who took both built projects far more advanced than either group had ever produced on its own.

The two programs did not merely coexist — combining them produced results beyond what each had achieved separately, and that amplified, greater-than-the-sum outcome is exactly what synergistic describes.

How Synergistic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

complementary

complementary: each part supplying what the other lacks so they work well together

reinforcing

reinforcing: strengthening one another's effect

amplifying

amplifying: making a result larger or stronger

Antonyms

counterproductive

counterproductive: working against the intended result

clashing

clashing: conflicting so badly that results suffer

How Strong Is It? — compatible → synergistic → transformative

compatible vs. synergistic

compatible vs. synergistic: Compatible is weaker: compatible tools simply work side by side without conflict, while a synergistic pairing actually multiplies what each one can do.

transformative vs. synergistic

transformative vs. synergistic: Transformative is stronger: a synergistic combination boosts results beyond the sum of the parts, but a transformative one creates something entirely new that neither part resembled.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — syn-

Prefix — syn-: together, with (Greek)

Root — erg

Root — erg: work (Greek ergon)

Suffix — -istic

Suffix — -istic: relating to, characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: Syn- (together) plus erg (work) literally builds "working together" — and the adjective describes combinations whose joint work yields more than the parts working apart.

Use the root in a new word: ergonomic
